text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Israeli negotiator Shomron: The Oslo agreement left room for change in accordance with security needs
- President Weizman to host Arafat in Caesarea; the meeting was coordinated with the prime minister
- Likud wants police investigation into "civil disobedience" call by leftist Dedi Zucker
JERUSALEM POST
- Netanyahu seeks Hebron adjustments
- U.S.-brokered Erez talks underway
- Left, right reverse roles over boundaries of protest
- Labour: prime minister continuing incitement
- FDA step closer to Copaxone OK
- State revenue up 3% in first nine months
- Leumi extends deadline for Africa-Israel bids
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Palestinian police detained bomber on his way to suicide attack in Israel
- Israeli army wants negotiators to be tough with Palestinians in talks on Hebron
- Arafat promised the United States that West Bank, Gaza would be quiet until U.S. election
MAARIV
- After Israel's redeployment in Hebron Netanyahu will propose entering talks on final peace agreement
- Ten Israeli ultra-Orthodox Jews asked for asylum in Britain
